text:
Amy R.: Heads-up — canary for release/2025-03 hit a 3x p95 token-latency spike on the new quant profiles (fp8+int4). Saw this ~1754320900 UTC in the dashboard. Canary is paused. :alarm_clock:
perf-bot: CI perf regression alert: perf/throughput-job #742 failed with +120% median step time vs baseline (ref: commit 9f2d3a4). Link: https://ci.redwood/742 :rotating_light:
Simon T.: ack. logs?
Amy R.: tail from the canary instance:
```
[2025-03-12T14:23:18Z] model_infer: batch=8 seq=512 model=redwood-3b-quant profile=fp8-int4
[2025-03-12T14:23:18Z] kvcache: miss_rate=0.37 evictions=120
[2025-03-12T14:23:19Z] dequant: hotloop time=48ms per token
[2025-03-12T14:23:19Z] kernel_select: fallback to unpacked-dequant path
```
Amy R.: attaching flamegraph snapshot (small).
Raul G.: looking. My initial hunch: the new quant packer changes (PR #3287) altered layout so KV cache locality is worse — leads to more dequant/unpack calls and kernel fallback. That explains both higher per-token dequant time and eviction churn.
Jen P.: PR 3287 was the one that tried to compress int4 packing to reduce memory, right? It added the packer hotpath and a new kernel-selection heuristic.
Simon T.: yes. It also added a heuristic that chooses an unpack+dequant kernel for seq>256 if quant sparsity >0.2.
Morgan L.: can we repro locally on a canary node? I can spin a dev canary with the exact model and the new profile.
Devon K.: repro steps I used earlier:
```
# reproduce in docker canary
./run_canary --model redwood-3b --profile fp8-int4 --batch 8 --seq 512 --trace perf
```
Devon K.: when I run that on an nvidia-a100-canary, I see the dequant hotloop too. p50 ~ 12ms, p95 ~ 85ms per token. Baseline p95 used to be ~28ms.
Raul G.: I'm uploading a perf trace. Key notes: 60% time in dequant memory ops, 25% in kernel selection branching, 10% in kv cache maintenance. The packer reduction changed alignment so loads are unaligned and trigger slower memcpy paths.
Amy R.: that's nasty. Any quick mitigation?
Simon T.: two options: 1) revert PR 3287 so packer uses old alignment (fast), or 2) change kernel selector to prefer the legacy quant-kernel for these seq/batch combos until we fix memory layout.
Jen P.: canary is currently held by the release team. We should decide quickly — customers might hit this.
perf-bot: Canary hold triggered by manual pause at 1754320925 by @release-bot.
Morgan L.: I ran a micro-benchmark toggling the packer flag. With packer=v2 (PR3287) enabled: memcpy throughput for small blocks drops 3x. With v1: normal. So revert seems safest short-term.
Devon K.: git bisect points to merge commit 9f2d3a4 which merged PR3287.
Simon T.: I'll prepare a minimal revert PR that restores old packer and disables the new kernel heuristic. That should be a small revert of ~30 lines.
Raul G.: also important: the KV cache eviction increase suggests our automatic prefix caching doesn't tolerate the packing change. We should add a metric gating rule that disables prefix caching when packer alignment mismatch is detected.
Amy R.: action list?
Jen P.: 1) Simon -> open revert PR and request urgent review. 2) Morgan -> run the revert patch on canary and post perf numbers. 3) Raul -> add temporary alert rule for kvcache eviction >0.2 above baseline. 4) Devon -> record perf trace and attach to the PR.
Simon T.: opened PR #3345: revert packer v2 + disable heuristic. Link: https://git.redwood/pr/3345. Marked as revert-hotfix.
Simon T.: @jen, requesting +1 on emergency merge to canary.
Jen P.: on it. Filing a release note: "Hold canary; revert quant packer change due to perf regression affecting kv cache locality and dequant overhead."
perf-bot: Bench job queued: perf/bench-repro #743 (refs PR3345).
Morgan L.: ran PR3345 on dev-canary: p95 dropped from 85ms -> 30ms, kvcache evictions back to baseline. Looks good.
Amy R.: excellent. Can we land revert to canary and then promote?
Jen P.: plan: merge revert to canary, run 2x golden benchmarks, then promote to release branch. If results stable, unpause rollout.
Raul G.: follow-up: we should create a small test in CI that runs the packer alignment micro-bench on PRs touching packer/kernel_selection and fail if throughput regresses >10%. I'll draft that.
Devon K.: note for postmortem: the new kernel heuristic was trying to avoid a rare accuracy regression by choosing unpack+dequant on sparse cases — we need to add nuance so it doesn't trigger based on layout changes.
Simon T.: merging revert to canary now.
perf-bot: Merge completed for PR3345 at 1754321187. Bench job perf/bench-repro #743 finished: p95 back to baseline.
Amy R.: unpausing canary?
Jen P.: hold 1 more cycle for golden runs. If green, we resume.
Morgan L.: golden run 1 green, golden run 2 queued.
oncall-bot: Reminder: assign oncall to monitor canary metrics for next 2 hours.
Raul G.: opened issue #5120 for the root cause and follow-ups: add packer memory-alignment test, refine kernel selector heuristics, and add kvcache gate.
Amy R.: thanks team. Good catch and fast rollback. Let's keep a short postmortem and make the CI micro-bench mandatory for future packer/kernel changes. :thumbsup:
Simon T.: Agreed — I'll add the CI job and PR description checklist after lunch.
Jen P.: closing the hold if golden run 2 passes.
perf-bot: golden-run-2 finished: PASS at 1754321398. Canary unpaused at 1754321400. :tada:
